{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:California cuisine|California cuisine]] | [[Cookbook:Seafood|Seafood]] | [[Cookbook:Appetizers|Appetizers]]

A ''ceviche'' is a seafood dish, originating in [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Peru|Peru]], that relies on acid rather than heat to cook the fish. This recipe adds a bit of a [[Cookbook:California cuisine|California]] twist by adding sliced [[Cookbook:Avocado|avocado]] to the dish.

== Ingredients ==
__NOTOC__
*1 [[Cookbook:Pound|pound]] (450 [[Cookbook:g|g]]) [[Cookbook:Scallop|bay scallops]]
*½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (125 [[Cookbook:mL|ml]]) [[Cookbook:Lemon Juice|lemon juice]] (about 3–4 lemons)
*4 red [[Cookbook:Bell Pepper|bell peppers]], roasted, peeled, and seeded
*2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] (30 ml) [[Cookbook:Balsamic vinegar|balsamic vinegar]]
*2 tablespoons (30 ml) extra-virgin [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|olive oil]]
*½ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] (2.5 ml) ground [[Cookbook:Cayenne pepper|cayenne pepper]]
*[[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]], to taste
*1 [[Cookbook:Avocado|avocado]], peeled and [[Cookbook:Slicing|sliced]]

==Procedure==
#In a non-reactive bowl, combine the scallops and lemon juice. Add more juice as needed to cover the scallops.
#Refrigerate, covered, and stir often for 2 hours, until the scallops become opaque.
#Combine the bell peppers, vinegar, oil, cayenne, and salt into a [[Cookbook:Food Processor|food processor]] or [[Cookbook:Blender|blender]], and [[Cookbook:Purée|purée]].
#To serve, spoon the sauce onto individual plates, drain the scallops, and place them on the sauce. [[Cookbook:Garnish|Garnish]] with slices of avocado.

==Notes, tips, and variations==
*For a more [[Cookbook:Southwestern cuisine|Southwestern]] flavor, replace ¼ cup lemon juice with [[Cookbook:Lime|lime juice]], and replace the bell peppers with New Mexico [[Cookbook:Chili Pepper|chili peppers]].

==Warnings==

* Eating raw seafood can cause illness if it is not fresh.
